forces.title: AI drives demand for advanced electronic components in data centers
forces.description: The rapid expansion of AI and the associated build-out of AI data centers are significantly boosting demand for electronic components and connectors. Beyond leading-edge chips and memory, this growth extends to applications and products utilizing advanced and mature nodes, such as workload-specific connectivity components, data flow components, and data center power electronics. Specific areas like photonics and power electronics are expected to experience rapid growth through 2030, serving as a key tailwind for the electronic components sector.
forces.source_title: The $2.3 trillion horizon: How AI is rewriting the semiconductor story

demand_drivers.description: The substantial capital expenditures by hyperscalers for AI infrastructure, particularly data centers, are driving demand for a diverse range of electronic components. This includes essential items like workload-specific connectivity and data flow components, as well as data center power electronics, crucial for managing the energy-intensive operations of AI systems.

pnl_drivers.description: Despite increased demand from AI, the average selling prices (ASPs) for advanced and mature electronic components are projected to decline. This trend may offset some of the revenue gains from higher volumes, putting pressure on profit margins for manufacturers of these specific components and connectors.

market_sizing.methodology: Analysis of AI's impact on semiconductor market segments, extending beyond leading-edge logic and memory to include 'advanced and mature nodes' applications and products. This segment is projected to contribute $100 billion in growth to the semiconductor market value by 2030, which encompasses workload-specific connectivity, data flow components, and data center power electronics, although average selling prices for these nodes are expected to fall.
